title: Halting after a nondeterministic choice
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program, with fixed oracle, input, and configuration predicate $G$. Suppose its instruction at state $l$ chooses between states $l_1$ and $l_0$. If the current configuration $(l,v,r)$ satisfies $G$, and every choice word of length $N$ from each of $(l_1,v,r)$ and $(l_0,v,r)$ leads to a halted configuration while all its earlier nonhalted configurations satisfy $G$, then every choice word of length $N+1$ from $(l,v,r)$ has those same halting and intermediate-configuration properties.
hypotheses_covered: A nondeterministic register program $A$, oracle, input, and predicate $G$
States $l,l_1,l_0$ with the instruction at $l$ choosing between $l_1$ and $l_0$
A register valuation $v$, result value $r$, and natural number $N$
The length-$N$ halting and intermediate-$G$ property holds from both successor configurations
